title: Magnetic Resonance Imaging of the Lumbar Spine

criteria.summary: Low back pain for at least 6 weeks
At least 6 weeks of conservative therapy without adequate improvement

passages.text: This policy applies to outpatient professional claims for MRI of the lumbar spine, CPT 72148 and 72158, with dates of service on or after April 1, 2026.
Lumbar spine MRI is considered medically necessary when criteria 3.1 and 3.2 are both met, or when criterion 3.3 is met.
The member has low back pain, with or without radicular symptoms, that has been present for at least 6 weeks.
The member has completed at least 6 weeks of conservative therapy, such as physical therapy, a home exercise program, or nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs, without adequate improvement.

A red flag is documented: a progressive neurological deficit, suspected cauda equina syndrome, a history of cancer, or suspected spinal infection. When a red flag is present, criteria 3.1 and 3.2 do not apply.

Documentation supporting each applicable criterion must be available in the medical record on request. Absence of documentation for a required criterion does not establish that the criterion was not met.
